summary: A 1969 note by Vint Cerf on the control links used between IMPs and between hosts. Its text indicates concern about interference with communication between IMPs. It is an early working note, not a standard.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 18 proposes using link 1 for control messages between hosts and link 0 for control messages between IMPs. The author says this would reduce delays caused by interference with IMP-to-IMP communication.

subtitle: A brief proposal assigning separate links to two kinds of control traffic.

tldr.problem: Communication between hosts could interfere with communication between IMPs.
tldr.mechanism: The note proposes link 1 for host-to-host control and link 0 for IMP-to-IMP control.
tldr.outcome: The author says this arrangement would facilitate host communication and reduce interference-related delays for IMP communication.

today: The unit metadata records RFC 18 as Unknown and lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The text is a short suggestion dated September 1969.

sections.title: Separate Links for Control Messages
sections.content:
The note suggests assigning link 1 to the host-to-host control link and link 0 to IMP-to-IMP control. It gives these as two distinct assignments for control communication.

The stated reason is to facilitate communication between hosts and reduce delays caused by interference with communication between IMPs.
sections.plainLanguage: The proposal gives host control messages and IMP control messages different links. Its stated aim is to make host communication easier and reduce interference-related delays for IMPs.

sections.title: A Short Suggestion
sections.content: RFC 18 consists of a brief suggestion and its rationale. It does not describe message formats, operating procedures or how the proposed link assignments would be implemented.
sections.plainLanguage: The note states which links to use and why. It does not explain the details of putting the proposal into practice.

sections.title: What the Note Establishes
sections.content: The text proposes link 1 for HOST-HOST control and link 0 for IMP-IMP control. It says that this arrangement would facilitate communication between hosts and reduce delays from interference with IMP-IMP communication.
sections.plainLanguage: The document records a two-link assignment proposal and the reason for it. It does not say whether the proposal was later adopted.
